target: Aku nggak bisa datang ke acara kantor besok malam.
english: I can't make it to the office event tomorrow night.
grammar: Heard everywhere in speech: nggak = tidak. Nggak bisa = tidak bisa (can't). In writing, use tidak.

target: Dia nggak suka kopi, jadi kami pesan teh manis.
english: He doesn't like coffee, so we ordered sweet tea.
grammar: Nggak is spoken tidak: nggak suka = tidak suka (doesn't like).

target: Kenapa kamu nggak bilang dari kemarin kalau mau pinjam motor?
english: Why didn't you say since yesterday that you wanted to borrow the motorbike?
grammar: Nggak bilang = tidak bilang. Nggak is how 'not' sounds in everyday talk.

target: Tenang, jalan ke stasiun nggak jauh, paling lima menit.
english: Relax, the walk to the station isn't far, five minutes tops.
grammar: Nggak jauh = tidak jauh (not far) — nggak is the everyday spoken 'not'.

target: Maaf ya, aku nggak sempat balas pesanmu tadi pagi.
english: Sorry, I didn't get a chance to reply to your message this morning.
grammar: Nggak sempat = tidak sempat (didn't get a chance). Spoken form of tidak.

target: Kalau hujan begini, dia biasanya nggak mau keluar rumah.
english: When it rains like this, he usually doesn't want to leave the house.
grammar: Nggak mau = tidak mau (doesn't want to) — you'll hear nggak far more than tidak.

target: Kata penjualnya, sambal di warung ini nggak terlalu pedas.
english: According to the seller, the sambal at this food stall isn't too spicy.
grammar: Nggak terlalu pedas = tidak terlalu pedas. Nggak is casual speech only.

target: Kamu nggak capek setelah lembur tiga hari berturut-turut?
english: Aren't you tired after working overtime three days in a row?
grammar: Nggak capek? = tidak capai? (not tired?) — everyday spoken register.

target: Mereka nggak jadi pindah ke Surabaya karena anaknya betah di sini.
english: They ended up not moving to Surabaya because their kid feels at home here.
grammar: Nggak jadi = tidak jadi: 'ended up not happening'. Nggak = spoken tidak.

target: Nggak apa-apa, besok kita coba lagi dari awal.
english: It's okay, tomorrow we'll try again from the start.
grammar: Nggak apa-apa = tidak apa-apa ('it's okay') — one of the most common spoken phrases.

target: Kamu udah makan belum? Aku baru mau pesan nasi goreng.
english: Have you eaten yet? I was just about to order fried rice.
grammar: Udah = sudah in speech: udah makan? = sudah makan? (eaten yet?)

target: Tenang, tiketnya udah aku bayar dari minggu lalu.
english: Relax, I already paid for the tickets last week.
grammar: Udah aku bayar = sudah saya bayar. Udah is how sudah sounds in conversation.

target: Dia udah berangkat ke bandara sejak jam lima pagi.
english: She already left for the airport at five in the morning.
grammar: Udah berangkat = sudah berangkat (already left). Spoken form; write sudah.

target: Laporanmu udah aku kirim ke bos tadi siang.
english: I already sent your report to the boss this afternoon.
grammar: Udah aku kirim = sudah saya kirim (already sent). Everyday spoken sudah.

target: Udah malam, ayo kita pulang sebelum hujan turun.
english: It's late already, come on, let's go home before the rain starts.
grammar: Udah malam = sudah malam ('it's late already'). Udah = spoken sudah.

target: Anak-anak udah tidur, jadi jangan berisik di ruang tamu.
english: The kids are already asleep, so don't be noisy in the living room.
grammar: Anak-anak udah tidur = sudah tidur. Udah is heard everywhere; sudah is written.

target: Filmnya udah mulai sepuluh menit yang lalu, kita telat.
english: The movie already started ten minutes ago, we're late.
grammar: Udah mulai = sudah mulai (already started) — spoken sudah.

target: Aku udah tiga kali telepon, tapi dia belum angkat juga.
english: I've already called three times, but she still hasn't picked up.
grammar: Udah tiga kali = sudah tiga kali (three times already). Casual speech.

target: Duduk di sini aja, dekat jendela biar adem.
english: Just sit here, near the window so it's cooler.
grammar: Aja = saja (just): di sini aja = di sini saja (just here).

target: Kalau bingung pilih menu, pesan yang biasa aja.
english: If you can't decide on the menu, just order the usual.
grammar: Yang biasa aja = yang biasa saja — 'just the usual'. Aja is spoken saja.

target: Kamu tanya aja langsung ke petugas di loket dua.
english: Just go ask the officer at counter two directly.
grammar: Tanya aja = tanya saja ('just ask'). Aja follows the word it limits.

target: Santai aja, rapatnya baru mulai jam dua nanti.
english: Just relax, the meeting doesn't start until two.
grammar: Santai aja = santai saja ('just relax'). Spoken form of saja.

target: Bilang aja ke ibu kalau kamu pulang telat malam ini.
english: Just tell Mom you're coming home late tonight.
grammar: Bilang aja = bilang saja ('just tell her'). Everyday speech; write saja.

target: Naik ojek aja dari stasiun, lebih cepat daripada jalan kaki.
english: Just take a motorbike taxi from the station, it's faster than walking.
grammar: Naik ojek aja = naik ojek saja ('just take an ojek'). Aja = spoken saja.

target: Ambil aja kuenya, masih banyak di dapur.
english: Go ahead and take the cake, there's still plenty in the kitchen.
grammar: Ambil aja = ambil saja ('go ahead, take it').

target: Kita ketemu di depan mal aja jam tujuh, ya?
english: Let's just meet in front of the mall at seven, okay?
grammar: Di depan mal aja = di depan mal saja ('let's just meet at the mall').

target: Macetnya parah banget tadi pagi di jalan ke kantor.
english: The traffic was really terrible this morning on the way to the office.
grammar: Banget = sekali/sangat: parah banget = parah sekali (really bad). Spoken only.

target: Kue buatan nenek enak banget, aku makan tiga potong.
english: Grandma's homemade cake is so good, I ate three slices.
grammar: Enak banget = enak sekali (so tasty). Banget follows the adjective.

target: Hari ini panas banget, jangan lupa bawa topi.
english: It's really hot today, don't forget to bring a hat.
grammar: Panas banget = panas sekali. Banget is everyday Jakarta-flavored speech.

target: Aku senang banget akhirnya kamu bisa ikut liburan bareng.
english: I'm so happy you can finally come along on the trip.
grammar: Senang banget = senang sekali (so happy). In writing use sangat/sekali.

target: Harga kamar hotel itu mahal banget waktu musim liburan.
english: That hotel room is really expensive during holiday season.
grammar: Mahal banget = mahal sekali (so expensive) — heard everywhere in speech.

target: Dia pintar banget matematika, selalu juara di kelasnya.
english: She's really good at math, always top of her class.
grammar: Pintar banget = pintar sekali. Banget = spoken 'very'.

target: Filmnya seru banget, kami sampai lupa waktu.
english: The movie was so exciting we completely lost track of time.
grammar: Seru banget = seru sekali (so much fun). Casual intensifier.

target: Kopi di kedai baru itu pahit banget menurutku.
english: The coffee at that new cafe is way too bitter, if you ask me.
grammar: Pahit banget = pahit sekali. In writing use sekali or sangat.

target: Gimana kabar orang tuamu di kampung?
english: How are your parents doing back in the village?
grammar: Gimana = bagaimana (how): gimana kabar…? = bagaimana kabar…?

target: Gimana kalau kita berangkat lebih pagi supaya tidak kena macet?
english: How about we leave earlier so we don't get stuck in traffic?
grammar: Gimana kalau…? = bagaimana kalau…? ('how about…?'). Spoken form.

target: Terus gimana hasil wawancara kerjamu kemarin?
english: So how did your job interview go yesterday?
grammar: Gimana hasilnya? = bagaimana hasilnya? Everyday spoken 'how'.

target: Gimana caranya pesan taksi lewat aplikasi ini?
english: How do you order a taxi through this app?
grammar: Gimana caranya? = bagaimana caranya? ('how do I…?'). Casual speech.

target: Kalau tiba-tiba hujan deras, gimana kita pulangnya?
english: If it suddenly pours, how are we getting home?
grammar: Gimana pulangnya? = bagaimana pulangnya? — spoken register.

target: Gimana rasanya tinggal jauh dari keluarga untuk pertama kali?
english: What's it like living far from family for the first time?
grammar: Gimana rasanya? = bagaimana rasanya? ('what's it like?').

target: Jangan bicara gitu ke adikmu, nanti dia sedih.
english: Don't talk like that to your little sibling, you'll make her sad.
grammar: Gitu = begitu (like that): bicara gitu = bicara begitu.

target: Kalau gitu, kita ketemu langsung di restoran jam delapan.
english: In that case, let's just meet at the restaurant at eight.
grammar: Kalau gitu = kalau begitu ('in that case'). Spoken shortening.

target: Cuacanya gini terus dari pagi, mendung tapi belum hujan.
english: The weather's been like this since morning, overcast but no rain yet.
grammar: Gini = begini (like this): cuacanya gini = the weather's like this.

target: Caranya gini: tekan tombol hijau, lalu pilih bahasa.
english: Here's how: press the green button, then choose a language.
grammar: Gini opens explanations: caranya gini = 'here's how'. Spoken begini.

target: Dari dulu memang gitu, pasar ini selalu ramai hari Minggu.
english: It's always been that way, this market is always packed on Sundays.

target: Dia memang suka bercanda gitu, jangan tersinggung.
english: He just likes to joke around like that, don't take offense.
grammar: Sentence-final gitu ≈ 'like that, you know'. Spoken begitu.

target: Kalau macet gini, lebih baik kita lewat jalan kecil.
english: With traffic jammed like this, we're better off taking the small roads.
grammar: Macet gini = macet begini (jammed like this). Gini/gitu = spoken begini/begitu.

target: Dia sering pulang larut gitu, ibunya sampai khawatir.
english: He often comes home late like that; his mom's getting worried.

target: Suaranya kayak penyanyi terkenal, padahal dia cuma karyawan biasa.
english: His voice is like a famous singer's, even though he's just a regular employee.
grammar: Kayak = seperti (like): kayak penyanyi = seperti penyanyi.

target: Rasanya kayak sup buatan ibuku di rumah.
english: It tastes like the soup my mom makes at home.

target: Kamu kelihatan lelah, kayak belum tidur semalaman.
english: You look worn out, like you haven't slept all night.

target: Langitnya gelap, kayaknya sebentar lagi hujan deras.
english: The sky's dark; looks like it's going to pour any minute.
grammar: Kayaknya = 'looks like/seems': kayaknya hujan = sepertinya hujan.

target: Kamu lagi ngapain di dapur malam-malam begini?
english: What are you doing in the kitchen this late at night?
grammar: Ngapain = spoken 'doing what?': lagi ngapain? = sedang apa?

target: Ngapain kamu bawa payung? Di luar cerah begini.
english: Why'd you bring an umbrella? It's perfectly sunny out.
grammar: Ngapain + verb = 'why bother': ngapain bawa payung? = why bring an umbrella?

target: Dia tanya aku lagi ngapain akhir pekan ini.
english: She asked what I was up to this weekend.
grammar: Lagi ngapain = 'up to what': spoken for sedang melakukan apa.

target: Ngapain beli yang mahal kalau yang murah juga bagus?
english: Why buy the expensive one when the cheap one is just as good?
grammar: Ngapain beli…? = 'why on earth buy…?' — casual why-bother question.

target: Anak-anak ngapain di halaman? Ramai sekali suaranya.
english: What are the kids doing in the yard? They're being so loud.
grammar: Anak-anak ngapain? = what are the kids doing? Spoken 'sedang apa'.

target: Ngapain menunggu lama-lama kalau bisa pesan lewat aplikasi?
english: Why wait around forever when you can order through the app?
grammar: Ngapain menunggu? = why bother waiting? Ngapain questions the point.

target: Bantu aku angkat kardus ini dong, berat sekali.
english: Come on, help me lift this box, it's really heavy.
grammar: Dong softens requests: bantu dong = 'come on, help me'. Spoken only.

target: Pelan-pelan dong, aku belum selesai mencatat alamatnya.
english: Slow down, will you — I haven't finished writing down the address.
grammar: Dong adds friendly pressure: pelan-pelan dong = 'slow down, will you'.

target: Cerita dong, liburanmu di Bali kemarin seru tidak?
english: Come on, tell me — was your Bali trip fun or not?
grammar: Dong invites: cerita dong = 'come on, tell me'.

target: Coba deh makan di warung sate dekat stasiun itu.
english: Go on, try eating at that satay stall near the station.
grammar: Deh nudges a suggestion: coba deh = 'go on, try it'.

target: Besok aku ganti uangmu, janji deh.
english: I'll pay you back tomorrow — I promise, really.
grammar: Sentence-final deh = 'really/I mean it': janji deh = I promise.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, aku berangkat sendiri deh.
english: If you're busy, fine, I'll just head out on my own then.
grammar: Deh marks giving in: aku sendiri deh = 'fine, I'll go alone then'.

target: Kok kamu belum siap? Kita harus berangkat sekarang.
english: How come you're not ready yet? We have to leave now.
grammar: Kok opens surprised questions: kok belum siap? = how come you're not ready?

target: Tenang, obatnya tidak pahit kok, anak kecil juga mau.
english: Don't worry, the medicine isn't bitter, really — even little kids take it.
grammar: Sentence-final kok reassures: tidak pahit kok = 'it's not bitter, really'.

target: Kok tiba-tiba listriknya mati, padahal tidak hujan?
english: How come the power suddenly went out when it isn't even raining?
grammar: Kok = puzzled 'how come': kok mati? = how come it went out?

target: Kamu ini kenapa sih, dari tadi diam terus?
english: What is it with you, you've been silent this whole time?
grammar: Sih sharpens a question: kenapa sih? = 'what IS it with you?'

target: Enak sih, tapi porsinya kecil untuk harga segitu.
english: It IS tasty, sure, but the portion is small for that price.
grammar: Sih concedes before a 'but': enak sih, tapi… = it IS tasty, but…

target: Siapa sih yang taruh sepatu basah di dalam rumah?
english: Who on earth put wet shoes inside the house?
grammar: Siapa sih…? = 'who on earth…?' — sih adds exasperation.

target: Entar sore aku mampir ke rumahmu bawa oleh-oleh.
english: Later this afternoon I'll drop by your place with some souvenirs.
grammar: Entar = nanti (later): entar sore = nanti sore.

target: Ntar dulu, aku masih cari kunci motor di tas.
english: Hold on a sec, I'm still looking for the motorbike key in my bag.
grammar: Ntar dulu = nanti dulu ('hold on a sec'). Ntar/entar = spoken nanti.

target: Jangan lupa entar malam kita telepon nenek bareng-bareng.
english: Don't forget, tonight we're calling Grandma together.

target: Kalau ntar hujan, acaranya pindah ke dalam aula.
english: If it rains later, the event moves inside the hall.

target: Dia emang jago masak, semua tamu minta tambah.
english: He really is a great cook — all the guests asked for seconds.
grammar: Emang = memang (really/indeed): emang jago = memang jago.

target: Emang kamu yakin tokonya buka hari libur begini?
english: Are you really sure the shop is open on a holiday like this?
grammar: Question-opening emang = memang: 'is it really true that…?'

target: Jalannya emang sempit, tapi pemandangannya luar biasa.
english: The road IS narrow, but the view is incredible.

target: Emang murah di pasar itu, tapi harus pintar menawar.
english: It really is cheap at that market, but you have to be good at bargaining.

target: Aku ke bioskop sama teman kantor habis pulang kerja.
english: I went to the movies with some coworkers after getting off work.
grammar: Spoken sama = dengan (with): sama teman = dengan teman.

target: Dia tinggal sama neneknya sejak kecil di Bogor.
english: She's lived with her grandmother in Bogor since she was little.

target: Jangan lupa foto sama keluarga sebelum pesawat berangkat.
english: Don't forget to take a photo with the family before the plane leaves.

target: Aku setuju sama pendapatmu soal jadwal baru itu.
english: I agree with your take on that new schedule.
grammar: After verbs, sama = dengan: setuju sama = setuju dengan (agree with).

target: Teman saya di Jakarta bilang, "Gue tunggu lo di depan halte."
english: My friend in Jakarta said, "I'll wait for you in front of the bus stop." (street-casual)
grammar: Jakarta slang pronouns: gue = saya, lo = kamu. Heard constantly; never use with elders.

target: Di film itu tokohnya berteriak, "Lo semua harus dengar gue!"
english: In that movie the character shouts, "All of you have to listen to me!" (street-casual)
grammar: Gue/lo (I/you) are Jakarta street pronouns — fine among close friends, rude to strangers.

target: Yuk berangkat sekarang, soalnya jalanan mulai ramai.
english: Come on, let's head out now, because the roads are getting busy.
grammar: Yuk invites: yuk berangkat = 'come on, let's go'. Softer cousin of ayo.

target: Kamu bawa payung kan? Langitnya mendung dari tadi.
english: You brought an umbrella, right? The sky's been overcast for a while.
grammar: Tag kan seeks agreement: bawa kan? = 'you brought it, right?'

target: Aku cuma mau tanya jadwal kereta terakhir ke Bogor.
english: I just want to ask about the last train to Bogor.

target: Nih, aku bawakan mangga dari kebun tetangga.
english: Here, I brought you some mangoes from the neighbor's garden.
grammar: Nih presents something at hand: nih = 'here (you go)'.

target: Tuh lihat, antreannya panjang sampai ke pintu depan.
english: Look at that — the line goes all the way to the front door.
grammar: Tuh points away from you: tuh lihat = 'look at that over there'.

target: Kita nonton film yang baru itu yuk, katanya seru.
english: Let's watch that new movie — people say it's great.
grammar: Nonton = spoken menonton (watch): nonton film = menonton film.

target: Aku ngobrol lama dengan sopir taksi soal harga bensin.
english: I chatted for a long time with the taxi driver about fuel prices.
grammar: Ngobrol = spoken 'to chat' (root obrol): ngobrol = mengobrol.

target: Habis makan siang, kita langsung rapat di lantai tiga ya.
english: After lunch we go straight into the meeting on the third floor, okay?

target: Duh, aku ketinggalan dompet di rumah lagi.
english: Ugh, I left my wallet at home again.

target: Motorku mogok di tengah jalan, aku dorong sampai bengkel.
english: My motorbike broke down mid-road; I pushed it all the way to the repair shop.

target: Telepon ibumu dulu, dia dari tadi cari kamu.
english: Call your mom first — she's been looking for you for a while.

target: Wah, rambutmu beda, potong di mana kemarin?
english: Whoa, your hair looks different — where did you get it cut?

target: Jangan buru-buru, keretanya baru datang setengah jam lagi.
english: No rush, the train doesn't arrive for another half hour.

target: Aku telat bangun, jadi lari ke halte tanpa sarapan.
english: I overslept, so I ran to the bus stop without breakfast.
grammar: Telat = spoken terlambat (late): telat bangun = overslept.

target: Titip beli air minum ya, aku tunggu di sini.
english: Grab me some drinking water, would you — I'll wait here.
grammar: Titip = 'get me…while you're at it': titip beli air = grab me some water.

target: Kabarnya kantor kita pindah gedung bulan depan, kamu tahu?
english: Word is our office is moving buildings next month — did you know?

target: Ayo cepat, filmnya mulai lima menit lagi.
english: Come on, hurry, the movie starts in five minutes.

target: Anakku susah makan sayur, maunya ayam goreng terus.
english: My kid won't eat vegetables — all he ever wants is fried chicken.

target: Tadi malam listrik mati dua jam, jadi kami mengobrol di teras.
english: Last night the power was out for two hours, so we chatted on the porch.

target: Besok libur, mendingan kita ke pantai pagi-pagi.
english: Tomorrow's a day off — better we hit the beach early.
grammar: Mendingan = spoken 'better (to)': mendingan pulang = better just go home.

target: Aku belum sempat cuci motor, kotornya minta ampun.
english: I haven't had a chance to wash the motorbike; it's unbelievably dirty.
grammar: Minta ampun after a quality = 'unbelievably': kotornya minta ampun.

target: Pelayan, tolong tambah sambal dan satu es teh manis.
english: Waiter, more sambal please, and one sweet iced tea.

target: Ternyata warung langgananku tutup, padahal aku sudah lapar sekali.
english: Turns out my usual food stall was closed, and I was already starving.

target: Kamu duluan ya, aku masih tunggu paket datang.
english: You go ahead — I'm still waiting for a package to arrive.
grammar: Duluan = spoken 'first/ahead': kamu duluan = you go first.

target: Hati-hati bawa motornya, rem belakangnya kurang pakem.
english: Careful riding the motorbike — the rear brake doesn't bite well.
grammar: Pakem = slangy 'grippy/sharp' for brakes: remnya pakem = the brakes bite well.

target: Seharian aku bolak-balik antara bank dan kantor pos.
english: I spent all day going back and forth between the bank and the post office.

target: Adikku baru lulus, sekarang sibuk cari kerja di Jakarta.
english: My little sister just graduated; now she's busy job-hunting in Jakarta.

target: Parkir di sini bayar berapa sejam, bang?
english: How much is parking here per hour, bro?
grammar: Bang (from abang) = 'bro/mister' for young men: bang, berapa? Casual address.

target: Bu, kembaliannya kurang dua ribu, tolong dihitung lagi.
english: Ma'am, the change is two thousand short — please count it again.

target: Malam ini aku menginap di rumah teman dekat kampus.
english: Tonight I'm staying over at a friend's place near campus.

target: Jangan main ponsel terus, matamu bisa sakit.
english: Stop playing on your phone all the time — your eyes will hurt.

target: Kapan-kapan kita coba kafe baru di ujung jalan itu.
english: Sometime we should try that new cafe at the end of the street.
grammar: Kapan-kapan = vague 'sometime': kapan-kapan kita ketemu = let's meet up sometime.

target: Tolong angkat jemuran, sepertinya sebentar lagi hujan.
english: Please bring in the laundry — looks like it's about to rain.

target: Aku baru sadar uang di dompetku tinggal dua puluh ribu.
english: I just realized I only have twenty thousand left in my wallet.

target: Katanya besok ada demo, jalan utama ditutup sampai sore.
english: They say there's a protest tomorrow — the main road is closed until evening.

target: Pak, lewat jalan belakang bisa tembus ke stasiun tidak?
english: Sir, does the back road cut through to the station?
grammar: Tembus = 'cuts through to': bisa tembus ke stasiun = comes out at the station.

target: Anak tetangga ribut terus dari pagi, aku jadi susah fokus.
english: The neighbor's kids have been rowdy since morning; now I can't focus.
grammar: Susah = spoken sulit: susah fokus = sulit fokus (hard to focus).

target: Santai, pesawat kita masih lama, ruang tunggunya juga nyaman.
english: Relax, our flight isn't for a while, and the waiting room is comfortable anyway.

target: Kamu dengar suara itu? Sepertinya ada kucing di atap.
english: Did you hear that sound? I think there's a cat on the roof.

target: Gara-gara hujan deras, sepatuku basah semua.
english: Thanks to the downpour, my shoes got completely soaked.
grammar: Gara-gara = 'because of' (with blame): gara-gara macet = all because of the jam.

target: Untung kamu ingatkan, aku hampir lupa bayar listrik bulan ini.
english: Good thing you reminded me — I almost forgot to pay the electric bill this month.
